newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cosmonauts decorated for Mir station fire bravery.
newsitem.headline: Cosmonauts decorated for Mir station fire bravery.

text.p: Two Russian cosmonauts were awarded medals on Tuesday for bravery in fighting a fire aboard the Mir space station which mission control officials played down as a minor incident at the time.
Valery Korzun and Alexander Kaleri were given medals usually awarded only to Russian firefighters, an Interior Ministry spokesman told Reuters.

A fire broke out aboard the Mir on February 23 when the cosmonauts tried to change a solid oxygen tube. Six cosmonauts, including an American and a German who were on the 11-year-old station at the the time, were forced to don gas masks.

The blaze was extinguished in minutes and nobody was hurt. But the incident, combined with other mishaps, combined to raise questions over Mir's safety, particularly from NASA in the United States, whose cooperation helps fund the station.
Korzun and Koleri returned to Earth with German astronaut Reinhold Ewald on March 2.
A mission control spokesman told Interfax news agency on Tuesday that Russians Vasily Tsibliev and Alexander Lazutkin and U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger were in good health on Mir.
The American is due to leave aboard the space shuttle Atlantis around May 17.
